intro: Mar Vista is Venice's quieter neighbor, with a walkable stretch of Venice Boulevard around Grand View, a Sunday farmers market and one of the best Japanese markets on the Westside. Its restaurant scene has grown fast, from Taiwanese comfort food on Grand View to a French bistro on Centinela.

places.w: The neighborhood's coffee hangout, roasting on site with playful drinks and a shaded patio. It has its own small parking lot.
places.o: A cardamom brown sugar latte and a croissant.

places.w: A big, calm cafe with a courtyard and long tables that make it one of the easiest places to work in Mar Vista.
A bright little cafe with a roomy patio, creative matcha drinks and a dog-friendly policy.
places.o: A seasonal matcha or the golden dirty chai.

places.w: A surf-themed cafe and shop with plenty of seating and outlets, plus occasional night markets.
places.o: A matcha latte with salted vanilla cold foam.

places.w: A French cafe with a relaxed patio and very large portions.
places.o: The breakfast croissant or the French toast.

places.w: A decades-old breakfast counter, formerly Maxwell's, with friendly service and short waits.
places.o: Eggs with the fruit side at the counter.

places.w: An airy, open-air cafe named after an Australian surf break. Easy lunches by day and a laid-back dinner with happy hour.
places.o: The Whirley Bowl at lunch, the burger at night. There's no Wi-Fi.

places.w: Mar Vista's 75-year-old corner grocery, rebuilt into a rustic Italian restaurant with a patio. One of the restaurants that defined LA in 2025.
places.o: The kale chicken salad at brunch, duck pappardelle or a pizza at dinner.

places.w: Taiwanese comfort food and the Mar Vista default for a weeknight dinner.
places.o: Scallion pancakes and the five-spice pork, then a drink next door at Accomplice.

places.w: A creative cocktail bar next to Little Fatty, with two back-to-back bars and a menu of a dozen house drinks.
places.o: Sit at the bar and watch the torched cocktails get made. Weekday happy hour.

places.w: A small raw bar and Southern California bistro from the former chef at Dudley Market, and one of the Westside's best new spots.
places.o: Walk in and start at the raw bar.

places.w: A neighborhood French bistro with an open kitchen counter and a reasonably priced tasting menu.
places.o: Roast chicken and potatoes with the Electric Fries, or the tasting menu at the counter.

places.w: Nayarit-style Mexican seafood that people drive across town for.
places.o: Pescado zarandeado to share, plus aguachile and shrimp tacos. Closed Tuesdays.

places.w: A Japanese supermarket with a busy food court and a bookstore full of manga and stationery.
places.o: Ramen or tempura in the food court, then snacks and mochi from the market.

places.w: A red taco truck in front of Mitsuwa known for loaded quesabirria with plenty of consommé.
places.o: The mini quesabirria tacos. Daytime only, closed Sundays.

places.a: Grand View Blvd and Venice Blvd
places.w: A Sunday morning market with produce, flowers, prepared food, music and kids' activities.
places.o: Go early for produce and stay for empanadas.

places.w: The neighborhood's big park, with a pool, tennis and basketball courts, a roller hockey rink, ball fields and shaded picnic areas.
places.o: Swim in the warm months or play tennis.
